page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a virtual machine instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores powered by Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz with one thread per core. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration includes AES instructions. Dedicated graphical processing units are absent. For high-speed local scratch space and high-throughput temporary I/O, the instance bundles 1888 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark analysis reflects strong multi-core processing power and memory subsystem performance. The D32plds_v6 achieves top-tier throughput in uncached memory transfers, generating 450.77 GB/sec in large-block read testing and 169.21 GB/sec in large-block write evaluations. In compute tests, the 32 dedicated physical cores reach strong scores in multi-core stress-ng workloads (66296.43), Clang software compilation (39729.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (330.6 GB/sec). Application benchmarks also show high throughput in data-handling environments, including 37222.49 on PassMark database operations and 61.98 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, accompanied by 53.68 GB/sec in static web serving.

The 2.0 GB per core ratio represents a leaner memory footprint compared to traditional 4:1 general-purpose allocations, providing an efficient compute-to-cost profile for tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark suites, as well as low execution rates on large-parameter language model prompt processing. Consequently, the D32plds_v6 is best aligned with multi-threaded build systems, web serving clusters, caching layers, and database workloads requiring high local NVMe throughput alongside dense parallel ARM execution.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a general-purpose ARM-based virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated physical cores on a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an integrated 1888 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance lacks dedicated GPU acceleration but delivers high hardware throughput, demonstrated by top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 450 GB/s for reads and 169 GB/s for writes, as well as superior results in PassMark database operations. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-threaded execution in stress-ng, Clang software builds, and Redis SET operations, while single-core metrics remain average. Given the lower RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high local storage throughput, the configuration offers dense multi-core compute capability without excess memory overhead. It is well suited for multi-threaded build systems, caching servers, web application clusters, and I/O-intensive database tasks.
